verifications.claim: Artemis II is a ~10-day crewed flight test of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "about a 10-day mission" (R2); "Duration: 10 days" (R3); "9 days, 1 hour" (R4); "nine-day trip" (R5); "about 10 days" (R6, R7)
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm ~10-day crewed test of SLS and Orion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled for April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 1 launch" (R1, R4); "By April 2026" / "Launch: April 2026" (R3); "April 2026" (R5, R6, R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm April 2026 launch schedule, with specifics matching.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will fly four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four astronauts" around Moon (all references)
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as four-astronaut lunar flyby mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will test life-support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "check important systems aboard Orion, including life support" (R1); "life support systems" (R3, R4, R5, R6, R7)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly listed as a key test objective across sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will test navigation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "onboard navigation sensors" in proximity ops (R1, R4); "navigation systems" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported in context of proximity operations and systems tests.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will test manual piloting.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "manually flew the spacecraft" / "manual control" (R1, R3, R4); "test the Orion's maneuvering system" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit manual piloting during proximity operations confirmed.

verifications.claim: Artemis II uses a "figure-8" free-return trajectory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "free-return trajectory" (all); "large figure-eight trajectory" (R6); looping path (R1, R4)
verifications.reasoning: Free-return confirmed everywhere; 'figure-8' specifically in R6 describing lunar swingby.

verifications.claim: Artemis II passes within ~4,100 miles of the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "more than 4,100 miles" / "about 4,000 miles" (R1); "4,067 mi" (R4); "4,100 miles" (R5); "4,000 and 6,000 miles" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Precise distance matches ~4,100 miles across sources.

verifications.claim: On Day 1 of Artemis II, the SLS rocket lifts off from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "blasted off... from Kennedy Space Center" Day 1 (R1); "Kennedy, LC-39B" (R4, etc.)
verifications.reasoning: Launch from KSC on Day 1 universally confirmed.

verifications.claim: On Day 1 of Artemis II, SLS places Orion in an initial high-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "two firings... large looping orbit... high-Earth orbit" Day 1 (R1); "high Earth orbit" (R4, R5)
verifications.reasoning: SLS upper stage firings place Orion in high-Earth orbit on Day 1.

verifications.claim: On Day 1 of Artemis II, the crew performs systems checks.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "systems checks" / "check out all systems" Day 1 (R1, R4, R5, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit Day 1 systems checks described.

verifications.claim: On Day 1 of Artemis II, the crew performs manual proximity operations.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "manually flew... close to the discarded stage" Day 1 (R1); "proximity operations demonstration" Day 1 (R4, R5)
verifications.reasoning: Specific Day 1 manual proximity ops with upper stage confirmed.

verifications.claim: On Day 2 of Artemis II, Orion fires its engines to leave Earth's orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "On Thursday, Orion will fire its engines to push it on a path toward the moon" (Day 2, R1); "TLI burn" Day 2 (R4, R5)
verifications.reasoning: Day 2 TLI burn to depart Earth orbit explicit.

verifications.claim: On Day 2 of Artemis II, Orion enters a "free-return" trajectory toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "free return trajectory" after Day 2 burn (R1, R4, R5)
verifications.reasoning: Day 2 burn places on free-return trajectory.

verifications.claim: During Days 3-6 of Artemis II, the spacecraft travels for roughly four days to reach the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four-day journey to the Moon" (R3); "four days to make the journey" Days 3-6 (R1, R4, R5)
verifications.reasoning: Consistent 4-day transit during Days 3-6.

verifications.claim: During Days 3-6 of Artemis II, the spacecraft performs trajectory corrections.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "outbound trajectory correction burns" (R4); "some course corrections" outbound (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Trajectory corrections during outbound leg (Days 3-6) confirmed.

verifications.claim: During the Lunar Flyby of Artemis II, the spacecraft swings around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "swing around the far side" / "passes behind the moon" (all)
verifications.reasoning: Lunar flyby around far side universally described.

verifications.claim: During Days 7-10 of Artemis II, the crew returns to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "four days to make the journey back" Days 7-10 (R1); return flight Days 7-10 (R4, R7)
verifications.reasoning: Return phase spans Days 7-10.

verifications.claim: During Days 7-10 of Artemis II, the crew performs a radiation shelter demo.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "planned demonstration of the spacecraft's radiation shielding was also canceled" (R4); "radiation shelter construction demo" planned Day 8 (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Planned but explicitly canceled per post-mission account (R4), contradicting 'will perform'.

verifications.claim: Artemis II splashes down in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (all)
verifications.reasoning: Universal confirmation of Pacific splashdown.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight to test Orion’s life-support systems in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: First crewed Orion / "test life support in deep space" (R1, etc.)
verifications.reasoning: First crewed deep-space Orion flight tests life support.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight to test Orion’s human-rated systems in deep space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first time humans... deep space" / systems tests (R1, R4)
verifications.reasoning: As first crewed deep-space Orion, tests human-rated systems.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II will manually pilot the spacecraft near the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) to evaluate handling.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "manually flew the spacecraft, nudging it close to the discarded stage [ICPS]" (R1); "proximity operations... using the spent ICPS" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit manual piloting near ICPS for handling evaluation.
